newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai soymeal, corn prices drop, attract demand.
newsitem.headline: Thai soymeal, corn prices drop, attract demand.

text.p: Thai soymeal and corn prices edged down from last week on rising supplies.
This, coupled with lower world prices, attracted some buying interest, trade sources said on Monday.
But actual buying was thin with buyers awaiting further dips in prices, they told Reuters.
Soymeal was quoted at around 9.00-9.30 baht ($0.36) a kg this week from 9.20-9.50 baht last week while corn was quoted at 4.10-4.20 baht a kg from 4.20-4.30 a week ago.
Industry sources said one major frozen poultry exporter expressed interest in buying 15,000-20,000 tonnes of U.S. or Argentine corn for April deliveries.
"I can confirm that there has been some enquiries. But I won't tell you the details. It could affect the prices," said a trader from one trading house tipped to handle the deal.
Another trader said complicated regulations on corn imports had dented buying interest despite traders' recent downward revision of 1996/97 corn output (July-June).
"Those who buy now would be exporters who can get a rebate on import tariffs under the government's export boosting measures," he said.
"The rest will just have to take a wait-and-see stance," he said.
Thailand in November cut import tariffs on corn to zero percent. But such tariff-free imports can be done only between February 20-June 30.
To protect local farmers, the govenment also stipulated that zero duty corn can be imported only when the local price is at or above 4.50 baht a kg.
Any imports not meeting those conditions would face a 20 percent import tariff.
The Thai Maize and Produce Traders Associations on Wednesday lowered its 1996/97 forecast for corn output to 3.96 million tonnes from a previous projection of 4.23 million.
Buying of soymeal was modest. "Sellers offers were at above $300 per tonne (c&f Bangkok) while buyers' price idea was around $270-290," said a trader from US trading house.
